description: Home to the Taj Mahal and the greatest concentration of Mughal-era monuments in India.

places.name: Taj Mahal — UNESCO World Heritage (Wonder of the World)
places.operating_hours: 30 min before sunrise to 30 min after sunset (closed Fridays)
places.description: Built by Emperor Shah Jahan (1631–1648) as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal. The world's greatest monument to love, the Taj Mahal is a UNESCO site and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.

places.name: Agra Fort — UNESCO World Heritage
places.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site built in red sandstone by Emperor Akbar (1565). Houses the stunning Jahangiri Mahal, Khas Mahal, and offers a Taj Mahal view from the Musamman Burj tower.

places.name: Fatehpur Sikri — UNESCO World Heritage (Mughal Ghost City)
places.description: Emperor Akbar's perfectly preserved Mughal capital (1569–1585), abandoned due to water shortage. A UNESCO site with stunning Panch Mahal, Jodha Bai's Palace, and Buland Darwaza.

places.name: Mehtab Bagh (Taj Mahal Moonlit Garden & Sunset View)
places.description: Moonlit garden built by Emperor Babur across the Yamuna from the Taj Mahal. Offers the finest sunset view of the Taj's iconic dome. Photographers' paradise.

places.name: Dasaprakash Restaurant (Famous Agra Sweets & South Indian)
places.description: Agra's most famous restaurant, celebrated for South Indian thalis, chaat, and especially the iconic Agra Petha (sweet made from ash gourd). Established 1956.

places.name: Panchi Petha Store (Finest Agra Petha since 1955)
places.address: Near Taj Mahal East Gate, Taj Nagari Phase 2, Agra
places.description: Agra's most renowned petha shop since 1955, famous for 100+ varieties of this iconic Mughal-era candy — from angoori and plain to chocolate and gulkand flavours.
